ai_summary: Scottish wind generation is performing strongly today, delivering an estimated Scottish wind output of 5.1 GW, which accounts for 50.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity, while overall GB wind output reaches 14.5 GW. This abundant renewable generation pushes Scottish carbon intensity down to an optimal 0 gCO2/kWh, compared against 79 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, severe north-south transmission bottlenecks continue to restrict export capability to southern demand centres. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has escalated to 68.6 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a direct constraint cost of about £2,030,146. Because this zero-carbon energy was turned down, fossil fuel generation was fired up elsewhere to compensate, consuming an estimated 13,042,550 m3 of gas and releasing an avoidable 24,026 tonnes CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualising today's expenditure produces an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of roughly £741 million. When socialised across typical annual British electricity demand, this constraint burden adds an estimated £2.60/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the acute financial and environmental necessity of accelerating cross-border grid reinforcement.
